title: Breakdown Engine: compute per-route/model/customer cost + latency attribution
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Background: The Console needs a reliable breakdown of inference cost and latency that can be sliced by customer (org), API route (text/generate/chat/embeddings), and model variant (model family + quantization/hardware profile). Current dashboards show aggregate spend and coarse latency p95/P99, but lack per-route attribution and don’t account for caching/batching effects. This ticket implements a dedicated "Breakdown Engine" in our analytics stack that computes attribution at minute granularity and feeds Console views, billing reconciliation jobs, and alerts.

Goals: Compute and store the following per (minute, org_id, route_id, model_variant, region):
- token_count_total: total input+output tokens charged
- cached_token_count: tokens served from prefix/KV cache (should be shown separately)
- compute_ms: GPU/CPU inference time attributed to these requests (derived from serving traces + sampled profiling)
- infra_cost_usd: cost allocated (GPU-hours prorated + host costs) for the compute_ms bucket
- token_cost_usd: inference-model license + per-token model cost where applicable
- total_cost_usd: infra_cost_usd + token_cost_usd + misc (IO)
- latency_p50_p95_p99: end-to-end latencies computed both raw and adjusted-for-batching

Approach:
1) Ingestion layer: existing telemetry pipeline (Kafka topic telemetry.requests.v2) will be augmented to include: route_id, model_variant, org_id, cached_tokens, request_token_count, response_token_count, serving_trace_id, serving_start_ts, serving_end_ts, backend_node_type. Producers: inference runtime will add model_variant and cached_tokens; edge proxy will add route_id and auth->org mapping.
2) Streaming computation: implement a Flink job (primary) that performs sessionized minute-window aggregation and attributes compute_ms and cached metrics. Flink chosen for low-latency windowing and mapping to existing streaming infra. The job will: parse telemetry events, correlate with sampled serving traces (join by serving_trace_id via a small keyed state), compute per-event compute_ms (serving_end_ts-serving_start_ts minus queueing), and emit minute aggregates to the downstream store.
3) Cost model: implement a small lookup service (model-cost-config) that exposes per-model-token cost and per-node GPU cost (usd_per_gpu_hour) and quantization multipliers. Flink job will call this as an in-memory broadcast state (configs are refreshed every 5 minutes). Infra cost attributed by GPU-minutes = compute_ms / 60000 * gpu_share where gpu_share accounts for batching (we estimate fair-share via request_token_count / total_tokens_in_batch when batch info is available).
4) Persistent stores: minute aggregates will be written to ClickHouse (high-cardinality materialized views) for Console queries and to BigQuery for monthly billing exports and heavy backfills. ClickHouse schema will include TTLs and rollup jobs (minute -> hourly -> daily).
5) Backfill and corrections: Spark batch job (EMR/Dataproc) will recompute historic windows for a given date range to correct drift or fix schema issues; a safe mode will mark corrected rows via a repaired_at column.
6) API and Console integration: expose an internal endpoint console-analytics/api/v1/breakdown that accepts query parameters (org_id, start_ts, end_ts, route_id*, model_variant*) and returns time-series arrays plus summed totals. Console team will render per-route/model/cost and enable per-customer cost drilldowns.

Key tradeoffs and mitigation:
- Accuracy vs latency: per-minute Flink aggregates provide near-real-time numbers but rely on sampling for serving traces. We will surface sampled_rate metadata and show a confidence band in UI. Backfills will provide ground-truth nightly reconciliations for billing export.
- Attribution for batching: exact fair-share attribution requires info from the serving runtime about batch composition. We'll add optional batch_metadata to telemetry and have the runtime emit it for sampled batches; otherwise use token-proportional heuristics.
- Storage costs: ClickHouse will hold high-cardinality minute data for 90 days with rollups; BigQuery will be the canonical long-term store for billing.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Open questions:
- Do we need per-token cost breakdown split by quantization level (int8 vs int4) or is model_variant sufficient? (ask runtime team)
- Sampling rate for serving traces: propose 5% to start; engineering to confirm overhead.
- SLA for analytic freshness: target 2 minutes end-to-end for Flink aggregates and 15 minutes for Console-visible data.

Links and artifacts:
- Technical spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Breakdown+Engine+Spec
- Prototype Jupyter and cost model notebook: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/prototype-breakdown-notebook
- Initial benchmark results (compute_ms vs trace samples): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/abcd1234/trace-sampling
acceptance_criteria: Flink streaming job deployed in staging consuming telemetry.requests.v2 and emitting minute aggregates to ClickHouse
Aggregates include token_count_total, cached_token_count, compute_ms, infra_cost_usd, token_cost_usd, total_cost_usd and latency_p50_p95_p99
Console internal API returns correct slices for sample orgs and matches Spark backfill within 0.5% for a 24h test window
Backfill job can recompute a full 30-day window and write corrected rows to BigQuery and ClickHouse
Monitoring: alert fires if Flink lag > 120s or commit failures > 1/minute, and dashboard shows sampled_rate and confidence bands
Documentation: runbook + architecture diagram added to Confluence and Console team has integration tests in their repo
data_schema_changes: New fields added to telemetry.requests.v2: route_id (string), model_variant (string), cached_tokens (int), request_token_count (int), response_token_count (int), serving_trace_id (string), serving_start_ts (iso8601), serving_end_ts (iso8601), batch_id (optional string), backend_node_type (string). ClickHouse minute_aggregates table columns: minute_ts, org_id, route_id, model_variant, region, token_count_total, cached_token_count, compute_ms, infra_cost_usd, token_cost_usd, total_cost_usd, latency_p50, latency_p95, latency_p99, sampled_rate, repaired_at
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy Flink job to staging with feature flag 'breakdown_v1'. 2) Canary to 10% of orgs for 48h, compare against existing coarse metrics and run consistency checks. 3) Enable for 50% for 24h, then full rollout. 4) Nightly backfill on first three days post-rollout to reconcile historical gaps. 5) After 2 weeks, switch Console to use breakdown API for all per-route/model views (toggleable).
operational_runbook: Runbook location: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Breakdown+Engine+Runbook. Key alerts: Flink_job_lag_gt_120s, ClickHouse_write_errors, Config_broadcast_staleness_gt_10m. Recovery steps: restart Flink taskmanager with state restore, switch Console to fallback aggregate API (legacy-cost-summary), run backfill for affected time range. On-call: infra-oncall -> analytics-sre. Post-incident: create incident ticket and run retrospective within 3 working days.
